catalogue_requests.reason: The catalogue has no class that starts a pump with the flow rate, target volume and mode already configured on the device. cap.actuation.pump.v1 requires flow_rate in uL/s and direction at invoke and reports dispensed_volume, while the clone's RUN takes no arguments and returns only a prompt character (harvardpump/pump.py:144-165, 216-217); binding it would have to invent a unit conversion and a volume reading. This extension sends RUN and reports the status named by the reply prompt.

The catalogue has no class that stops a pump. cap.motion.stop.v1 is a motion-axis stop with a deceleration input and does not bind the fluid.pump resource kind; the clone's STP is the native stop (harvardpump/pump.py:216-218). This extension sends STP, is the R2 safe-state action, and reports the status named by the reply prompt.

The catalogue has no class that selects the forward or reverse direction of a pump as a standalone setting. cap.actuation.pump.v1 carries a direction input only as part of a run at a declared flow rate and reports a dispensed volume, neither of which the clone's DIR command does (harvardpump/pump.py:222-225). This extension sends DIR INF or DIR REF and reports the status named by the reply prompt.

notes:
PASSED ON THE FAKE BACKEND ONLY by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/bgamari__harvard-syringe-pump --backend fake; G1-G9 all passed and the check report contains no finding or warning. Evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. The gate digest is the digest line the last check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package. Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model, reviewed_by is null. No hardware was attached, the serial port was never opened, and nothing here ran on a pump.

SHAPE: the card's decision family-config and helper SerialDriver were confirmed. The clone's Model44, which the GTK UI instantiates on /dev/ttyUSB0 (harvardpump_ui:10, 136), sends text commands with a carriage return (harvardpump/pump.py:140-142); the words DIA, RAT, TGT, DEL, VER, MOD, DIR, RUN and STP all occur in the clone, so the command table of the serial bridge expresses the wire syntax. The bridge itself opens pyserial for the hardware view; the clone is Python 2 and is never imported or run. The reply frame is LF, reply text ending at CR, a digit and a prompt character (harvardpump/pump.py:144-165); the driver sets terminator CR and parses values and prompts with regular expressions.

COVERED: reads diameter (DIA), flow rate (RAT), target volume (TGT), mode (MOD), accumulated volume (DEL) and version (VER); writes diameter, flow_rate, target_volume and mode; actions x-cap.bgamari.start_pump.v1 (RUN), x-cap.bgamari.set_direction.v1 (DIR INF/DIR REF) and the safe-state x-cap.bgamari.stop_pump.v1 (STP); the e-stop also sends STP. The flow rate is always sent in the mL/min range (RAT <value> MM) and the resulting accumulated volume is in mL, the unit the UI's range table gives that range (harvardpump_ui:60-65).

NOT COVERED: (1) The other three flow-rate ranges (uL/min, uL/hr, mL/hr, harvardpump/pump.py:229-233) are not exposed; the RAT read has to know the value's unit, so a front-panel range change would make the read fail its unit pattern rather than silently report the wrong unit. (2) The Model22 class is not driven; the UI instantiates Model44 (harvardpump_ui:10, 136). (3) clear_volume_accum (CLD), clear_target (TGT 0) and reverse (DIR REV) are not exposed as actions; the same STP and DIR commands are covered through stop and set_direction. (4) The upstream _format_float truncates its six-decimal text to six characters (harvardpump/pump.py:171-173); a str.format command template cannot reproduce that truncation, so this driver sends at most six significant digits. The command words, spaces and the MM range token are unchanged. (5) The upstream get_mode lowercases the reply (harvardpump/pump.py:253-256); this SerialDriver state exposes the raw PMP/VOL token because a read parser cannot map its case, and the driver writes the uppercase tokens of the clone. (6) The hardware backend is the serial bridge's pyserial path and was never opened.

LIMITS: no text of the clone states a numeric diameter, flow-rate or target-volume range. _format_float raises only above 1e6 and truncates the text, which is an encoder behavior, and the GTK spin-button maxima are UI defaults, not device bounds; therefore the three writes use Limit.operator_required and are refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until a site overlay supplies the range of the installed syringe. site-limits.example.json is an example only (0.1-50 mm, 0-10 mL/min, 0-10 mL) and is not a statement about any syringe. The mode allowed set PMP/VOL and the direction allowed set INF/REF come from the commands of the clone (harvardpump/pump.py:245-251, 222-225).

SAFETY: a pump that dispenses liquid is at least R2, above the card's R0 floor. The clone text names no independent hardware emergency stop, interlock, door or watchdog, so estop_physical_ref is not set; the @estop sends STP and the safe-state action x-cap.bgamari.stop_pump.v1 sends STP, which is the R2 stop path accepted by SAFE-045. The loader refuses this R2 hardware backend while reviewed_by is null.

FAKE: the clone has no simulator, test suite or recorded session (task.mock_strategy.upstream_tests is null and its hints are empty), so the preferred transcript was not available. fake.py is an in-memory pyserial-like transport that answers only the command words the driver sends, keeps the diameter, flow rate, target volume, mode, direction and running state, reproduces the reply frame and prompt of the clone, and marks every number as a placeholder. Gate G7 (transport mode) checks the command mnemonics against the clone, not the fake class.
